### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **48** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cloud-connection/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**32** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 303aef069ebdfee276d4b053a11c1bc2e8fa0e90`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cloud-connection/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **156** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 303aef069ebdfee276d4b053a11c1bc2e8fa0e90` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3e0152e3a74d636ffede54ce555c28ff51459a0a` — the merge of head `8989149c2dc0f4f9acd7f8c820e4b7ac89a1c663` into base `303aef069ebdfee276d4b053a11c1bc2e8fa0e90`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3e0152e3a74d636ffede54ce555c28ff51459a0a && git checkout 3e0152e3a74d636ffede54ce555c28ff51459a0a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 303aef069ebdfee276d4b053a11c1bc2e8fa0e90 8989149c2dc0f4f9acd7f8c820e4b7ac89a1c663 && git checkout -B drift-repro 303aef069ebdfee276d4b053a11c1bc2e8fa0e90 && git merge --no-ff 8989149c2dc0f4f9acd7f8c820e4b7ac89a1c663

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 303aef069ebdfee276d4b053a11c1bc2e8fa0e90
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 303aef069ebdfee276d4b053a11c1bc2e8fa0e90` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ac8ce968761bf36751f5a5c60ff6cc884524aca7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-access-upgrade.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/local-manifest-source.ts, packages/cloud-connection/package.json, packages/cloud-connection/vitest.config.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/access-upgrade-check.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/access-upgrade-check.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/package/install.ts, packages/cli/test/package-install-access-upgrade.test.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, pnpm-lock.yaml + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/access-upgrade-report.ts (U1: `collectAccessUpgradeFindings`, `accessUpgradeSummary`, `accessUpgradeDedupKey`, `hasAccessUpgradeFindings`), packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts (`createSecurityCatalogReader`), packages/metadata-core/src/meta-write-capability.ts (`walledCatalogWriteVerdict`), packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts (the walled anchor, `:1624`), packages/cloud-connection/src/install-local-principal.fixtures.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`refuseSecurityCatalogNameConflicts` `:3081`, `getPackage` `:6172`, `installPackage` `:5960`), packages/objectql/src/security-catalog-namespace.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (`refuseEnvironmentHeldSecurityCatalogNames` `:2517`), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts (`listDeclaredRules` `:1063`), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts (`:384`, `:700`), packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts (`SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` `:113`), packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts (`:4494`), scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs and scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs and scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs read at `origin/main` (the clone's working tree is 286 commits behind main and predates ruling A). The prose faces, judged under ②: .changeset/24446-u2-marketplace-access-upgrade-refusal.md, content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx, content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx, content/docs/references/api/contract.mdx, content/docs/references/api/error-code-ledger.mdx.

### ① Derived judgments

Line numbers are the head's unless a file is named as new (then the diff's).

1. **Placement of the pre-write check — right.** `handleInstall` converts the body forward once at `:1686` (moved up from its old place under step 3, pure, so nothing changes in what registers) and runs step 2c at `:1700–1706` only when `findConflict === 'marketplace'`; the first write stays `manifestService.register` at `:1727`, and the ledger write at `:1771`. `findConflict` (`:2832`) answers `marketplace` for a live ledger entry or for a package the registry holds with no ledger entry and no boot snapshot (the orphaned-install branch), `none` for a fresh install, `user-code` refused at step 2. So the check runs on every managed re-install path through this door and never on a fresh install: `mountWithV1` pins `check` uncalled on the version-1 install for all 34 cases, and the `unmanaged` mode leaves at `:1583` before step 2 (a copy, never an upgrade, by ADR-0131 D6). On the orphaned branch `previousEntry` is null and the check falls back to the registry's own record of the package (`registeredManifest`, access-upgrade-check.ts `:236–240`, `registry.getPackage(id).manifest`), which the plugin-security suite drives over a real ObjectQL ("version 1 read from the registry"). The D5e gate (2b) stays ahead of 2c, so a caller can meet two refusals in sequence; both are 409, both carry `confirmWith`, and the CLI renders each.

2. **Delta-only refusal and the projection — right, with two notes for ③.** The check (`createAccessUpgradeCheck`, `:249–274`) runs U1's `collectAccessUpgradeFindings` unchanged twice and answers `accessUpgradeDelta(before, after)`. The projection replaces exactly P's registry items: `projectCatalog` (`:133–149`) drops entries whose `packageId === P` and adds the incoming `permissions`/`positions`/`capabilities` as entries stamped `packageId: P` with no `_provenance`, so `isTenantAuthored` keeps reading them as managed; `projectSharingRules` (`:152–167`) does the same for the declared rules; `projectEngine` (`:170–189`) answers an incoming object with the registry's field set less what P's previous version declared plus the incoming declaration, answers an object P dropped as absent, and passes `find` through so the ledger and `sys_sharing_rule` rows are never projected. The previous version is the ledger entry's body converted forward (`:2459`) or the registry's record. `accessUpgradeDelta` (`:198–233`) subtracts orphans and collisions by whole-value identity and keeps only the grown candidates, missing names and fields of the other three kinds, so a finding that predates the upgrade or that another package caused never blocks (pinned in both suites, ablation 2 reddened the pin). Two notes: (a) `projectCatalog.list` also drops an entry of ANOTHER holder whose name the incoming manifest ships (`!names.has(e.name)`), so a customer clone bearing the incoming name disappears from the projected run instead of surfacing as a collision; see ③ E2. (b) an orphan row with `active: true` (a dead switch, not a switch-off) is also a finding and refuses: ruling item 1 lists orphans without qualification, so this is within the ruling, and `describeAccessFindings` names it as "carries a switch".

3. **The confirm token — right.** `findingSet = accessUpgradeDedupKey(delta)`: a sha256 over `accessUpgradeSummary`, which carries every field of every finding (type, name, packageId, candidates with their binding positions, rowId and organization of a collision, each missing name, each uncovered field), 32 hex characters. The door (`:2486–2494`) recomputes the set on the confirming call and admits only `typeof token === 'string' && token === findingSet`; a bare `true` fails the type test, a stale token fails the comparison and is refused again with the fresh set and a sentence saying why (pinned: token installs and is recorded; `true`; stale). The confirmation `{ findingSet, confirmedBy: userId, confirmedAt }` is written into the ledger entry only when findings existed (`:1763`); the CONTROL pin reads it absent. One property to know, not a defect: the digest excludes the incoming version string, so two incoming versions producing the identical finding set share a token — "the token confirms exactly the findings it names" is what the PR says and what it does.

4. **Walled operator-gated, `single` the administrator — right.** `refuseWalledCatalogPackage` (`:1470`, body at `:3950`) runs after the id gate and before 1c, 1e, 1d, 2, 2b and 2c; `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` admits only the `PLATFORM_ADMIN` rung under `group`/`isolated`; its refusal body is `403 FORBIDDEN` with `details: { manifestId }` and nothing else, so no finding reaches a tenant administrator and the check never runs for one (pinned: `check` not called, `details.findings` undefined, for both postures and all four types). Under `single` the `manage_metadata` holder (`admin_full_access`) reaches 2c and their token admits. R4 in the os-dev-report measured D12 itself on a production walled serve (tenant owner 403 at the capability gate; with `manage_metadata` in their organization, 403 from D12; no finding; no "stopped" line). Pin-precision note, not a defect: the door suite's ctx has no `getKernel`, so `resolveAdmissionTenancyPosture` (`:3753`) answers undefined and `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` is inert there; the suite's tenant administrator is refused one gate earlier, by `requireInstallCapability`, because under a requested wall no stored grant anchors standing (`resolve-authz-context.ts:1624`, `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE`). The asserted outcome is the same (403 FORBIDDEN, nothing shown, check uncalled), and D12 was measured in R4; the docblock's "refused by the D12 wall" names the later of the two gates.

5. **A stopped check fails closed — right.** U1's three stops (`scan-unreadable`, `catalog-unreadable`, `sharing-unreadable`), the check's own `unbound` (before `start()` binds the engine and the metadata service) and a throw from the service all answer `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (a standard-catalog member, `errors.zod.ts:113`, the 503 derivation) with `details.reading`, and nothing is registered or written (pinned at the door with the ledger offline; pinned in plugin-security for `scan-unreadable` and `unbound`).

6. **No `security.accessUpgradeCheck` in the composition — fail-open with one `warn`, acceptable as measured and GO'd, with one residual escalated (③ E1).** The measurement (6355301005 §2, "Fail closed") proposed exactly this limb and the seat's GO (6355317159) is "build as measured". Weighed: ruling 6259332195 item 2 binds the access class at marketplace upgrade; ADR-0126 wall 3 says an upgrade never writes the ledger and never un-makes a choice. The door writes no ledger row in either limb, so wall 3's literal clause holds; what the absent limb cannot do is see whether a choice is un-made in effect. In a composition without plugin-security no permission set, position or capability is enforced, so there is no access choice of those three types whose effect an upgrade could un-make, and refusing every re-install there would make plugin-security a hard dependency of the marketplace door, a composition decision outside this card. The residual: the absence test is "no `security.accessUpgradeCheck` service" (`:2451`), which is "no plugin-security", not "no access enforcement". plugin-sharing composes without plugin-security (`sharing-plugin.ts:384` depends on objectql alone; `:700` probes `security` optionally) and enforces the `sharing_rule` switch-off itself, so in that composition a vendor rename of a switched-off rule would go unchecked and the warn line's sentence ("enforces no switch-off ... an upgrade could un-make") over-claims. Every shipped composition in this repository composes `SecurityPlugin` (`serve.ts:4494`), so the residual is theoretical here. A present service without a `check` function is also read as absent (`:2452`); a narrower limb, same disposition.

7. **No runtime dependency on plugin-security — right.** `cloud-connection/package.json` `dependencies` are unchanged; `@objectstack/plugin-security` enters `devDependencies` only (and the lockfile gains the one link). The door imports nothing from it: the service name is a local constant (`:349`) and the answer is a local structural type (`:355–372`); `vitest.config.ts` aliases the package to this checkout's source for the door suite, the pattern the file's other entries follow. No cycle: plugin-security depends on neither cloud-connection nor runtime; cloud-connection already depends on runtime.

8. **Every accept-set and public-surface change, named.** Narrowing: `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local` on a managed re-install now answers `409 ACCESS_UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` (or `503`) where it used to install — declared `(narrowing)`, banner present. Widenings, each right: the `confirmAccessUpgrade` request-body key (a string token; `true` is accepted syntactically and refused semantically); `error.details.{manifestId, findingSet, findings[], confirmWith{body, cli}}` with `findings[].kind` in `re-enablement | orphan | collision | broken-reference | uncovered-deny` and a `describe` line each; the optional `accessUpgradeConfirmation` on the exported `InstalledManifestEntry` (`local-manifest-source.ts:88`); plugin-security's three value exports and five type exports (`index.ts:141–155`) and the `security.accessUpgradeCheck` service registered in `init()` (`security-plugin.ts:1776`) over sources resolved per call; the CLI's `--confirm-access-upgrade` string flag and its refusal rendering (every `describe` line, then the exact retry); the new ledger row. Cosmetic: the CLI prints `details.findingSet` unguarded, so a runtime that omitted it would print the word `undefined`.

9. **Tests, as pinned.** Door: 4 types × (single 409, single CONTROL, isolated and group operator 409, isolated and group tenant administrator 403, isolated CONTROL) = 28, plus token/true/stale, predates, stopped 503, no-service 200 — 34. No `group` CONTROL at the door; `group` and `isolated` share `postureEnforcesWall`, and the isolated CONTROL covers the path. plugin-security: 15 over a real ObjectQL and SQL driver with the plugin's own registration, including the two clone-body cases the card names. CLI: 3. Ablations: three, each red then restored. The 43 check-runs on the head conclude success or skipped-by-design; none fails.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on both carriers — right.** Read against `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` at `origin/main`: the key at line start in the fixed spelling, the value token `yes` first after the colon, the arm `(narrowing)` as the next non-blank parenthetical in the closed spelling, trailing reasoning tolerated, the key named once per line, no open backtick span. The changeset line and the PR-body line are byte-identical. A diff that widens (a service, exports, a code, a body key, a flag) and narrows (the door's answer on re-install) is exactly the `yes (narrowing)` combination the reader documents.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` — right.** Nothing a metadata author writes changes: an error code is wire vocabulary, `confirmAccessUpgrade` is a request-body key, `accessUpgradeConfirmation` is a runtime ledger-file field, the service and exports are runtime, the flag is CLI. No `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` baseline moves (the diff touches none); `Spec property liveness` is green.
- **`patch` on `cloud-connection`, `plugin-security`, `spec`, `cli` — right.** Under maintainer ruling A (2026-10-21, #25105; AGENTS.md at `origin/main` `:1091–1093`), the level follows the metadata-protocol kind alone: `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". The gate's own self-test pins `yes (widening)` + `none` and `no (narrowing)` + `none` to the `none-clean` lane; `Check Changeset` on this head concluded success. The clone's working-tree copy of the gate and of AGENTS.md predates ruling A (there `yes` took at least `minor`); the review read the main versions, and the house rule the brief states is ruling A.
- **The BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 marker — both present, both right.** `**BREAKING** —` opens the body's first paragraph; the marker is `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, which is honest: no metadata schema key is added, removed, renamed or re-shaped, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite and no tombstone exists; the "migration" the body states is a runtime ceremony on the same call (re-send with the finding set's token), not a rewrite of consumer code or metadata, which is the one thing that category refuses. The gate at `origin/main` reads the `(narrowing)` arm as a breaking signal and found its marker; `Lint & Repo Gates` is green. A narrowing WITHOUT the banner or the marker would be a defect: during the launch window those two are the only carriers of breaking-ness, since the level no longer carries it.
- **The ADR-0112 ledger row — right.** `ACCESS_UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` under `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, the package whose Hono route stamps it (D3: registered under the owning package, a deliberate reviewable act); SCREAMING_SNAKE; domain-prefixed; `standardSynonymOf` maps it to no standard member, and the ledger test (`error-code-ledger.test.ts`, run in Test Core) admits it unwaived; the row's comment carries the meaning, the status, the pre-write guarantee and why neither `UNIQUE_SCOPE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` (per-index decisions) nor a conflict code (which no confirmation lifts) fits, the same reasoning `INSTALL_MODE_NOT_PERMITTED` was admitted on. 409 is the D5e gate's status and the request is well formed; no 5xx limb. ADR-0112's "registering a code widens the published face and is a Clause-② change" is declared. The three generated reference pages regenerate (`+342 more`), and `check:generated` was run.
- **Size and tier.** +1,471 / −9 over 18 files, under 3,000; 0 of 18 paths on the governed register at `origin/main` (`docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, `.github/workflows/**`); `packages/spec` is not a register row. Ordinary queue landing once accepted. The `--paths` recogniser reads the schema face off `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`; the Scope line above holds the narrowing floor, which contains it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Seat GO (a), the CLI flag in U2's surface — done.** `--confirm-access-upgrade TOKEN` sends the token verbatim as `confirmAccessUpgrade`, is absent from the body without the flag, and the refusal prints every `describe` line and the exact retry; three pins. `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` documents the flag and its semantics in the same words as the door.
- **Seat GO (b), `POST /api/v1/packages` with `overwrite` — correctly held.** `runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` is untouched; the dev's out-of-scope line names it as the seat's follow-up. The service that door will call is exported and shaped for it (`check({ packageId, manifest, previousManifest? })` answers `clean | findings | stopped`), so the second door calls the same check, not a copy.
- **Seat GO (c), a token and never a bare `true` — done** (① item 3).
- **Dev's added limit** ("an object the incoming manifest adds that the registry does not yet hold is judged on its declared fields only") — answered: immaterial. No customer-authored set or `sys_sharing_rule` row can yet name an object that did not exist, and the uncovered-deny check pairs a managed set with a customer set granting the same object by name, so neither kind can fire on a new object.
- **Dev's out-of-scope (2)** (no example app declares `@objectstack/organizations`; R4 needed temporary edits) — an observation from U1 repeated; not this card's.
- **Dev's out-of-scope (3)** (`cli.mdx`'s options table omits `--install-mode`) — answered: a note suffices under Prime Directive #10 (a delivered flag that one table does not list is not an advertised-undelivered capability); the seat may file a docs card.
- **Open questions in the report: none.** Deviations from the GO: none found; the file surface is the measured one plus the CLI test, the vitest alias and the lockfile link the devDependency needs.
- **E1 — escalated to the seat, not a FAIL:** the absent-service fail-open limb (① item 6). The seat should rule whether the door's absence test stays "no plugin-security" (as measured and GO'd) or widens to refuse `503` when a `sharingRules` service is composed and no check is, so a sharing-rule switch-off is never upgraded unchecked in a plugin-sharing-only composition. One line at `:2451` plus a pin either way.
- **E2 — escalated to the seat, not a FAIL:** catalog-name collisions at the door (① item 2a). The projected catalog replaces, rather than reports, an environment-authored (customer clone) position or permission set whose name the incoming version ships. The registry's package door refuses that second holder at registration (`registry.ts:3081`, environment holders included, called from `installPackage` `:5960`): on the inline branch that is `422 PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED` before any write (door `:1735`); on the cloud-fetched branch the lenient register writes the ledger entry anyway (`:1745`, "whether it should is a separate decision, not made here") and the next cold boot refuses (`plugin.ts:2517`). That hazard predates this PR and is outside the GO, but ruling item 1 names same-name collisions and U1's GO said "the pre-write check is U2's". Recommend the seat decide whether the follow-up card (the one holding `POST /api/v1/packages`) adds a collision finding kind for the three catalog types at both doors, or records that registration's refusal is the pre-write answer and the cloud branch's lenient write is a separate card.
- **E3 — stays open on the card, as the GO already says:** the `repo:cloud` request 6355241020. The GO lifted it as a precondition for the framework door; if cloud has an install path of its own, it calls `security.accessUpgradeCheck` before its first write in cloud's follow-up.
- **Docs drift check** (PR comment 6355823895) is advisory and names the generated pages this PR regenerated; `cli.mdx`'s "Who sees it" sentence matches the door's admission.
